text:
elaine: Heads up — hit a weird case. SI partner submitted a lead (via intake form) for AcmeCorp, but our sales rep already had a small POC deal in Hub. Who owns outreach and next steps?

miguel: Thanks for flagging. Is the SI the primary contact for the account now or just the technical introducer?

elaine: SI was an introducer only — they have the infrastructure team contact, but no commercial exec. Sales has an SDR thread open and a $10k POC opportunity in the pipeline.

tanya: My gut: sales should keep commercial ownership, SI gets delivery/enablement. But we need a deterministic rule so it isn't subjective.

samir: Agreed. Proposal: ownership flows to whichever party submitted the earliest recorded opportunity in our CRM. If SI intake is after an open opp with owner assigned, that owner keeps it.

marc: Two exceptions we should codify: 1) SI is Tier-1 or has a signed referral MSA that grants co-sell rights for accounts they source; 2) SI has a signed funded PO or reseller agreement for that account.

elaine: Good call. Also need a tie-breaker when both claim simultaneously (e.g., handshake emails same day).

miguel: Tie-breaker idea: 24h claim window where we default to the account's commercial team unless the SI provides signed intent (email/PO) within that window. If still ambiguous, route to Partnerships queue for manual adjudication.

samir: For automation, we can use a "broker_flag" and "claim_ts" fields in the intake record. Pseudocode for dedupe: 
```
-- incoming lead L, account A
if exists(opportunity for A with owner != null and op.created_ts < L.submitted_ts) then owner = opportunity.owner
else if L.partner_tier == 'tier-1' and L.has_msa then owner = partner.owner
else if within_24h_multiple_claims(A) then create_partnerships_case(A, claims)
else owner = sales_queue.round_robin()
```

tanya: Love the pseudocode. Also add a mapping rule: match on normalized domains + normalized legal entities. We had duplicates because acmecorp vs acme corp inc matched poorly.

marc: Add product-fit dimension too — if it's infra-only (on-prem/private), SI gets priority for lead-handling for initial assessment; commercial handoff remains to sales once scope is validated.

ops-bot: Note: Created ticket PARTNER-789 in partnerships-workflow for manual adjudication (assignee: tanya).

elaine: Perfect. A couple of operational requests: 1) update the intake form with a required field 'commercial-owner-if-any', 2) add a checkbox for 'signed-referral-msas' so we can filter quickly.

miguel: I'll own the intake form update. Will also add the broker_flag to the intake webhook payload. ETA: EOD Friday.

tanya: I'll update the partnerships runbook with the tie-breaker rules and examples (include sample emails that count as "signed intent").

samir: Ops: can we add a nightly dedupe job that normalizes company names and flags likely duplicates? We should surface a confidence score in the ticket so Partnerships can triage quickly.

marc: Yes — add confidence thresholds: auto-merge at >= 0.98, manual review 0.7-0.98, ignore below 0.7. Use domain > name matching prioritization.

elaine: Thanks team. Last ask: when we close an adjudication, log the reason tag (ownership: sales | partner | split) and the evidence (link to email or PO) — helps for future audits.

miguel: Agreed, will include fields in webhook and the ticket creation flow.

tanya: I'll run a 30-day pilot for these rules on a subset of entering leads (US & EMEA). Will report back with metrics (time-to-claim, manual-adjudications%).

samir: If pilot looks good, let's bake into the intake SLA and update the partner-facing docs so SIs know the rules upfront.

elaine: Great. Closing loop: partnerships ticket PARTNER-789 will have the pilot checklist. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
